notes:
Quorum: token-weighted commit-reveal voting on Sepolia.

Token. src/Quorum.sol declares name "Quorum", symbol "QRM" and decimals 18 as constants, matching the token block above. Its constructor takes no arguments and mints totalSupply (1_000_000_000 ether = 10^27 minor units) to msg.sender, so the whole supply lands on the deploying factory and no constructor moves it afterwards. There is no mint, burn, owner, admin, pause or upgrade path: the only balance-changing functions are transfer/transferFrom/approve, and totalSupply is a compile-time constant, so it is fixed for the life of the contract.

Application contract. src/CommitRevealVote.sol is the single application contract and is listed first and last, since it has no project-internal dependencies. Its constructor is `constructor(address token_)`, one nonpayable address parameter, which is filled by $token so the contract is bound to the launch token deployed in this same launch. The constructor reverts with InvalidToken() on the zero address and assigns the immutable `token`; it makes no external calls and reads no msg.sender, so nothing about the deploying factory is captured as a privileged identity.

Why there is no $owner reference. CommitRevealVote has no owner, admin, fee recipient, treasury or any other privileged role, and therefore no constructor parameter that a project owner could occupy. Ownership for this launch is carried by policy alone; this manifest deliberately names no wallet and hard-codes no address. The absence of an $owner argument here reflects the accepted source, not an omission.

No initialization calls are required. Every parameter the contract needs is set in the constructor: the token address is the contract's only configuration, and proposal timing is supplied per proposal by the caller of openProposal(bytes32 titleHash, uint64 commitDeadline, uint64 revealDeadline) rather than being configured at deployment. Anyone may open a proposal; there is no allowlist to seed.

Dependency order. Only one project contract exists, so the ordering requirement is trivially satisfied and no $contract: reference appears. Should further contracts be added later, they would need to follow CommitRevealVote in this list to reference it.

Constructor argument audit. Exactly one argument is declared above and exactly one is declared in the source. It is address-typed, which is the only argument type into which a reference may be placed, and $token is a backward reference to the launch token, which is deployed before the application contracts. No static words, no bytes32, no uint and no bool arguments are used anywhere in this manifest.

Pool. Paired against native ETH on Sepolia, expressed as the zero address, with fee 3000, tickSpacing 60 and initialPrice "79228162514264337593543950336", the sqrtPriceX96 for a 1:1 ratio. The pool has no hook. These are the policy's standard pool parameters and are not a statement about what QRM is worth.

Runtime and opcode profile. CommitRevealVote uses no proxy, no DELEGATECALL, no CALLCODE and no SELFDESTRUCT; its only external interaction is transfer/transferFrom on the immutable token address, guarded by a nonReentrant mutex and ordered checks-effects-interactions, with explicit return-value checks so a token returning false is treated as a failure. It is not payable and holds only the QRM that voters lock while a ballot is outstanding.

Scope. This manifest describes the accepted tree at src/Quorum.sol and src/CommitRevealVote.sol with ABI exports under docs/abi/. It carries no supply, allocation, owner, chain, policy-version or artifact-hash fields; those belong to policy, attestation and the deployer, which bind the published commit and creation bytecode after this stage. These notes are explanatory and confer no deployment authority.
